subject: Acme redlines: MSA + Order Form — IP, training, and telemetry
messages:
From: Susan Lambert <susan.lambert@acme.com>

Cc: Acme Legal <legal@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redlines on MSA + Order Form — IP & Training

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the draft MSA and order form. Our legal team attached redlines (Acme_Redlines_20260310.docx) that focus on three things we need clarified/changed before procurement can proceed:

1) Output ownership: We need explicit assignment of ownership for customer-provided prompts and outputs that Acme uses to build product features (examples: knowledge base generator, output used in end-user UI).
2) Training / model use: No customer data should be used to train or improve models (including aggregate fine-tuning) unless we opt in per-account and receive a separate commercial term.
3) Feedback & telemetry license: Any telemetry/feedback that Redwood collects must be governed by a narrow, non-exclusive license limited to service improvements and debugging; no commercial reuse.

We called out telemetry/telemetry retention and auditability (SOC 2 evidence) as part of the procurement checklist. Please let us know if Redwood can accept those redlines or propose alternative language. We would like to resolve this prior to the pricing/PO step — our procurement team needs clear IP language.

DocuSign or next steps: legal@acme.com is on copy — happy to schedule a quick call if it helps.

Thanks,
Susan
VP, Product at Acme Corporation

Susan — thanks for the clear note and for sending the redlines. I attached a short response draft (proposed_response_draft.docx) that lays out a path we think is acceptable. High-level thoughts here so we have context before legal digs in: 

- Output ownership: We understand the ask for assignment where Acme directly productizes the outputs. We typically offer a customer-first approach for outputs while preserving our ability to improve and operate the service. That said, we can outline explicit productization carve-outs and propose a limited assignment/transfer for outputs used in downstream product features (with commercial terms).
- Training: We can support an account-level opt-out for training with an associated fee/technical restrictions (there are latency/cost implications). For large enterprise accounts we can offer a stronger training blackout for a fee or via Dedicated/Private deployment.
- Telemetry/feedback: We're ok narrowing the license to service improvement and debugging; we'll not use telemetry for commercial resale. Need legal to confirm the exact wording for "service improvement" and the retention/audit commitments.

Laura — looping you and Marissa in for redline suggestions and to confirm if the proposed commercial path (assignment for productized outputs + paid training opt-out) is acceptable from risk and revenue views.

Next steps I propose: 1) Legal proposes alternate clause text (Laura), 2) Product (Marissa) confirms the operational impact and any Dedicated/Private options to support training restrictions, 3) I'll coordinate procurement timeline with Acme.

Susan — would you be available for a 30-min call Thursday 3/12? We'll bring legal + product.

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Karthik / Marissa — I reviewed Acme's redlines and sketched three alternative approaches with pros/cons; happy to discuss on the Thursday call. Refer to attached redline_solution_v2.pdf for inline edits. Summary: 

Option A — Explicit assignment for productized outputs
- Contract language: customer shall own outputs and may assign/transfer rights for outputs used in customer products; Redwood retains a narrow operational license to provide the service and to debug.
- Pros: Clears procurement ask, minimal ambiguity for productization.
- Cons: Limits Redwood's downstream reuse for model benchmarking; needs telemetry carve-outs.

Option B — Customer-first license with operational carve-outs
- Contract language: Redwood grants customer broad rights to use outputs; Redwood retains perpetual, royalty-free right to use de-identified, aggregated telemetry for model improvements, subject to data protection and opt-out mechanisms.
- Pros: Preserves model improvement pipeline and avoids full assignment.
- Cons: Procurement may push back; need clear definition of "de-identified" and auditability.

Option C — Training opt-out + Dedicated/Private alternative
- Contract language: Customer may elect (in order form) to prohibit use of data for training; this triggers either a fee or requirement to move to Dedicated/Private deployment with technical isolation.
- Pros: Commercially pragmatic and operationally enforceable.
- Cons: Additional cost; timeline/ops impacts.

Telem/Feedback suggestion: Narrow the feedback license to "service improvements and bug fixes" and include a retention window (e.g., 90 days for raw telemetry, longer for aggregated metrics). Offer SOC 2 logs and a data flows diagram as evidence.

Marissa — please confirm if we can operationalize Option C (approx cost delta for training opt-out and whether Dedicated is required for a hard technical block). Karthik — if Acme wants firm assignment language, we should ask procurement for a revenue/compensation tradeoff.

I'll be on the Thursday 3/12 10:00 PT slot; please confirm.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Associate General Counsel, Redwood Inference

Laura will provide final clause text that limits Redwood's operational rights to debugging and service delivery only. This should satisfy your procurement ask while preserving a narrow runway for Redwood to operate the service.

2) Training: Acme may elect an account-level training opt-out in the order form. There are two implementation paths: (i) training opt-out with a commercial fee (we'll provide an estimate once product confirms), or (ii) Dedicated/Private deployment with stricter technical isolation and no training. Marissa — can you confirm the delta for the training opt-out fee and whether Dedicated is required for a hard technical block?

3) Telemetry & feedback license: Redwood will narrow the license to "service improvements and debugging" only; raw telemetry retention window will be documented (proposed 90 days for raw logs, 24 months for aggregated metrics). We'll provide SOC 2 evidence and a data flow diagram to Acme Legal.

4) Next steps & timeline: Laura will deliver language by EOD Mon 3/15. Marissa to provide implementation/cost by Tue 3/16. Karthik will coordinate a procurement-ready redline and DocuSign timeline — target to finalize order form the week of 3/22 if all parties align.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this.
